findings.title: Start the hunter's missile cooldown only after a successful launch
findings.claim: hunterThink updates lastLaunch before the requested launch is applied. A crew laser hit can raise enemy Weapons from level 1 to 2 between those operations, causing the launch to be refused while still consuming its cooldown.
findings.evidence: plan L1188–1189 updates lastLaunch when constructing input; plan L1217–1218 thinks first, then applies crew commands before enemy commands; plan L892 and L913 allow the crew hit to invalidate the launch. Spec L202 defines the missile launch rule.
findings.why: After repairing Weapons, the hunter can remain unable to launch until 30 seconds after a missile it never launched. The isolated hunterThink test at plan L1025–1031 misses this ordering failure.
findings.fix: Update lastLaunch only when an enemy missile actually launches. Add a stepDuel regression where the crew damages enemy Weapons from 1 to 2 on its proposed launch tick; assert that no missile launches and lastLaunch remains unchanged.

findings.title: Give pursuit steering a deterministic turn when the target is directly behind
findings.claim: The cross-product-only steering returns zero for both directly ahead and directly astern. With a lead point directly behind, the hunter neither turns nor thrusts. Missile pursuit has the same blind spot.
findings.evidence: plan L403–404 defines sideOf as the cross-product sign; plan L1171–1173 uses it directly for ship pursuit, and plan L1180 uses it for missile pursuit. Spec L201 requires steering toward the lead point; spec L202 requires missile pursuit toward the delayed position.
findings.why: For heading north and target displacement (0, 300), the cross product is zero and the dot product is negative, yielding turn=0 and thrust=0 despite needing a half-turn. Only avoidance has a tie-break, at plan L1169.
findings.fix: For pursuit, distinguish zero-cross-product ahead from astern using the dot product. Choose a fixed turn direction when the target is astern, preserving zero turn ahead. Test this for both ship and missile steering.

findings.title: Expire missiles at the end of their 480th flight tick
findings.claim: A missile survives all 480 flight ticks and is destroyed only on call 481, leaving the laser frozen one extra tick.
findings.evidence: plan L192–193 defines 360 fuel ticks and 480 total lifetime ticks; plan L789–790 increments age and expires only when age > MISSILE_LIFE_TICKS. Plan L1220–1223 advances weapon clocks after missile processing. Spec L147 requires six seconds of thrust followed by two seconds of coasting and self-destruction.
findings.why: After eight seconds, the missile remains present with age=480, so laserFrozen still returns true. The proposed lifetime test at plan L659–668 permits this and does not assert the ending cause or exact tick.
findings.fix: Perform all 480 movement/contact ticks, then expire any surviving missile before that tick's weapon clocks. Do not merely change the pre-movement comparison to >=, which would omit the final movement tick. Add exact lifetime, fuel-boundary, expiry-cause, and laser-unfreeze assertions.

findings.title: Test the resumed full-charge hold timer without a fresh press
findings.claim: The tests do not establish Decision 4's central behavior: a frozen full charge resumes its remaining hold timer even while fireHeld is false.
findings.evidence: plan L41 states this decision and plan L924 implements it. The missile-end test at plan L727–739 immediately proceeds to a fresh press/release; the unattended test at plan L536–548 uses only a partial charge. Spec L160 explicitly requires the frozen full charge to resume its hold timer.
findings.why: These tests would still pass if the hold timer incorrectly required Fire to remain held, allowing a preserved full charge to last indefinitely.
findings.fix: Freeze a full charge with a nonzero hold timer, verify that both clocks remain unchanged while frozen, then end the missile or re-attend without pressing Fire. Assert venting after exactly the remaining attended, unfrozen ticks and no automatic recharge.
